intro.label: // ABOUT THE GAME
intro.title: What is Borrowed Shapes?
intro.paragraph_1: Borrowed Shapes is a 3D cooperative household adventure about a family trying to spend one meaningful Sunday together after years of drifting apart.
intro.paragraph_2: Players take the shapes of everyday objects representing David, Sarah, Alex, Lily, and their loyal dog Buddy. Each object has different strengths, speed, size, and weight, so every room asks the team to switch roles, plan together, and help one another.
intro.paragraph_3: The journey moves through familiar spaces such as the Kitchen, Bedroom, Bathroom, Basement, and Living Room. Simple household activities — cleaning, cooking, repairing, organizing, and finding a way forward — become cooperative challenges. After each room’s main tasks, the space shifts into a chaotic final challenge before the next door can be unlocked.

hero.title: Hall of Fame
hero.subtitle: Meet the creators, builders, testers, and storytellers behind Borrowed Shapes.

team.title: Meet the Crew
team.subtitle: Each member carries a role, a responsibility, and a piece of the world we built together.

descriptions.sm: Manage Scrum activities, coordinate Sprint planning and reviews, monitor project progress, manage Product Backlog priorities, communicate with stakeholders, and ensure the project follows Scrum practices throughout development.
descriptions.tl: Design technical architecture for web systems and gameplay mechanics, manage database and networking structures, review technical implementation, and maintain overall system stability and code quality.
descriptions.doc: Prepare, maintain, organize, and standardize project reports, technical documentation, formatting guidelines, and document version control.
descriptions.dl: Design and maintain technical diagrams including class diagrams, sequence diagrams, activity diagrams, use case diagrams, workflows, database relationship diagrams, and system architecture visualizations to support analysis and development activities.
descriptions.qa: Execute testing activities, validate Sprint deliverables, track defects, verify gameplay and system quality, and ensure completed features satisfy the Definition of Done (DoD).
descriptions.des: Design UI/UX layouts, gameplay visuals, interaction flows, visual assets, and maintain visual consistency across game and web systems.

before_contact.title: Before You Contact Us
before_contact.description: To save time waiting for a response, you can quickly check some of the items below before submitting a support request.
items: Check if you are using the latest game version on the Download page.
Try logging out and logging back in if the error is related to your account or session.
Search the Forum or Wiki to see if your issue has already been resolved.
Prepare screenshots or error messages if available.

bug_report.title: When reporting a bug, please include
items: The game version or website URL where the error occurred.
The device, operating system, and browser you are using.
Clear steps to reproduce the bug.
Screenshots, a short video, or error message content if available.
The time the error occurred and the related account if the error involves profiles, downloads, or play history.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What should I do if I can't log in?
faq.a1: Please check your email, password, and internet connection, then try logging in again. If you use Google Login, make sure your Google account is active. If the error persists, please send a description of the error and a screenshot to the development team.
faq.q2: What should I do if I can't download the game?
faq.a2: Please check your internet connection, available storage on your device, and try downloading again from the Download page. If the download link has expired or is not working, return to the Download page to get a new link.
faq.q3: How do I report inappropriate content on the forum?
faq.a3: Please use the report function if available on the post or comment. The report will be sent to the moderation team for review according to community guidelines.
faq.q4: Where should I send gameplay feedback or new map suggestions?
faq.a4: You can create a post in the Forum with the Suggestion type or discuss it in community threads. Clear feedback with specific examples will help the development team evaluate it better.

contact.title: Contact Borrowed Shapes
contact.description: Need help with your account, downloads, forum, achievements, gameplay results, or a bug report? Contact the Borrowed Shapes team through the project’s official channel.

card.title: Contact us on Facebook
card.description: The fastest way to send questions, bug reports, or feedback to the Borrowed Shapes team is through the project’s official Facebook page.
card.secondaryNote: If you are reporting a bug, please describe the issue clearly and include reproduction steps, browser/device information, and screenshots if available.

contact.privacyReminder: Do not send passwords, verification codes, access tokens, refresh tokens, or sensitive information through messages. The Borrowed Shapes team will never ask for your password.

faq.q: I cannot log in. What should I do?
faq.a: Check your email/password, try the forgot password flow, or sign in again with Google if you use Google Login.

faq.q: I cannot download the game. What should I do?
faq.a: Go to the Download page, choose the recommended/active version, and try again with a stable internet connection.

faq.q: How do I report inappropriate content?
faq.a: Use the report feature on the website if available, or send the relevant link/content through the official contact channel.
